1.t: All praise is for Allah Who has revealed the Book to His servant, allowing no crookedness in it
1.tr: Alhamdu lillaahil lazeee anzala 'alaa 'abdihil kitaaba Wa-lam yaj'al lahoo 'iwajaa

2.t: ˹making it˺ perfectly upright, to warn ˹the disbelievers˺ of a severe torment from Him; to give good news to the believers—who do good—that they will have a fine reward
2.tr: Qaiyimal liyunzira ba'asan shadeedam mil ladunhu Wa-yubashshiral mu'mineenal lazeena ya'maloonas saalihaati anna lahum ajran hasanaa

3.t: in which they will remain forever

4.t: and to warn those who claim, “Allah has offspring.”
4.tr: Wa-yunziral lazeena qaalut takhazal laahu waladaa

5.t: They have no knowledge of this, nor did their forefathers. What a terrible claim that comes out of their mouths! They say nothing but lies
5.tr: Maa lahum bihee min 'ilminw Wa-laa li-aabaaa'ihim; kaburat kalimatan takhruju min afwaahihim; iny yaqooloona illaa kazibaa

6.t: Now, perhaps you ˹O Prophet˺ will grieve yourself to death over their denial, if they ˹continue to˺ disbelieve in this message
6.tr: Fala'allaka baakhi'un nafsaka 'alaaa aasaarihim il lam yu'minoo bihaazal hadeesi asafaa

7.t: We have indeed made whatever is on earth as an adornment for it, in order to test which of them is best in deeds
7.tr: Innaa ja'alnaa ma 'alal ardi zeenatal lahaa linabluwahum ayyuhum ahsanu 'amalaa

8.t: And We will certainly reduce whatever is on it to barren ground

9.t: Have you ˹O Prophet˺ thought that the people of the cave and the plaque were ˹the only˺ wonders of Our signs
9.tr: Am hasibta anna Ashaabal Kahfi war-Raqeemi kaanoo min Aayaatinaa 'ajabaa

10.t: ˹Remember˺ when those youths took refuge in the cave, and said, “Our Lord! Grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us rightly through our ordeal.”
10.tr: Iz awal fityatu ilal Kahfi faqaaloo Rabbanaaa aatinaa mil ladunka rahmatanw Wa-haiyi' lanaa min amrinaa rashadaa

11.t: So We caused them to fall into a dead sleep in the cave for many years

12.t: then We raised them so We may show which of the two groups would make a better estimation of the length of their stay
12.tr: Summa ba'asnaahum lina'lama ayyul hizbaini ahsaa limaa labisooo amadaa

13.t: We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ their story in truth. They were youths who truly believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance
13.tr: Nahnu naqussu 'alaika naba-ahum bilhaqq; innahum fityatun aamanoo bi-Rabbihim Wa-zidnaahum hudaa

14.t: And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and declared, “Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him, or we would truly be uttering an outrageous lie.”
14.tr: Wa-rabatnaa 'alaa quloo-bihim iz qaamoo faqaaloo Rabbunaa Rabbus samaawaati wal-ardi lan nad'uwa min dooniheee ilaahal laqad qulnaaa izan shatataa

15.t: ˹Then they said to one another,˺ “These people of ours have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not produce a clear proof of them? Who then does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah
15.tr: Haaa'ulaaa'i qawmunat takhazoo min dooniheee aalihatal law laa yaatoona 'alaihim bisultaanim baiyin; faman azlamu mimmaniftaraa 'alal laahi kazibaa

16.t: Since you have distanced yourselves from them and what they worship besides Allah, take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will extend His mercy to you and accommodate you in your ordeal.”
16.tr: Wa-izi'tazal tumoohum Wa-maa ya'budoona illal laaha faawooo ilal kahfi yanshur lakum Rabbukum mir rahmatihee Wa-yuhaiyi' lakum min amrikum mirfaqa

17.t: And you would have seen the sun, as it rose, inclining away from their cave to the right, and as it set, declining away from them to the left, while they lay in its open space. That is one of the signs of Allah. Whoever Allah guides is truly guided. But whoever He leaves to stray, you will never find for them a guiding mentor
17.tr: Wa-tarash shamsa izaa tala'at tazaawaru 'an kahfihim zaatal yameeni Wa-izaa gharabat taqriduhum zaatash shimaali Wa-hum fee fajwatim minh; zaalika min Aayaatil laah; maien yahdil laahu fahuwal muhtad, Wa-maien yudlil falan tajida lahoo waliyyam murshidaa

18.t: And you would have thought they were awake, though they were asleep. We turned them over, to the right and left, while their dog stretched his forelegs at the entrance. Had you looked at them, you would have certainly fled away from them, filled with horror
18.tr: Wa-tahsabuhum ayqaazanw Wa-hum ruqood; Wa-nuqallibuhum zaatal yameeni Wa-zaatash shimaali Wa-kalbuhum baasitun ziraa'ayhi bilwaseed; lawit tala'ta 'alaihim la-wallaita minhum firaaranw Wa-lamuli'ta minhum rubaa

19.t: And so We awakened them so that they might question one another. One of them exclaimed, “How long have you remained ˹asleep˺?” Some replied, “Perhaps a day, or part of a day.” They said ˹to one another˺, “Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with these silver coins of yours to the city, and let him find which food is the purest, and then bring you provisions from it. Let him be ˹exceptionally˺ cautious, and do not let him give you away
19.tr: Wa-kazaalika ba'asnaahum liyatasaaa'aloo bainahum; qaala qaaa'ilum minhum kam labistum qaaloo labisnaa yawman aw ba'da yawm; qaaloo Rabbukum a'lamu bimaa labistum fab'asooo ahadakum biwariqikum haazihee ilal madeenati falyanzur ayyuhaaa azkaa ta'aaman falyaatikum birizqim minhu walyatalattaf Wa-laa yush'iranna bikum ahadaa

20.t: For, indeed, if they find out about you, they will stone you ˹to death˺, or force you back into their faith, and then you will never succeed.”
20.tr: Innahum ien yazharoo 'alaikum yarjumookum aw yu'eedookum fee millatihim Wa-lan tuflihooo izan abadaa

21.t: That is how We caused them to be discovered so that their people might know that Allah’s promise ˹of resurrection˺ is true and that there is no doubt about the Hour. When the people disputed with each other about the case of the youth ˹after their death˺, some proposed, “Build a structure around them. Their Lord knows best about them.” Those who prevailed in the matter said, “We will surely build a place of worship over them.”
21.tr: Wa-kazaalika a'sarnaa 'alaihim liya'lamooo anna wa'dal laahi haqqunw Wa-annas Saa'ata laa raiba feehaa iz yatanaaza'oona bainahum amrahum faqaalub noo 'alaihim bunyaanaa; Rabbuhum a'lamu bihim; qaalal lazeena ghalaboo 'alaaa amrihim lanat-takhizanna 'alaihim masjidaa

22.t: Some will say, “They were three, their dog was the fourth,” while others will say, “They were five, their dog was the sixth,” ˹only˺ guessing blindly. And others will say, “They were seven and their dog was the eighth.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “My Lord knows best their ˹exact˺ number. Only a few people know as well.” So do not argue about them except with sure knowledge, nor consult any of those ˹who debate˺ about them
22.tr: Sa-yaqooloona salaasatur raabi'uhum kalbuhum Wa-yaqooloona khamsatun saadisuhum kalbuhum rajmam bilghaib; Wa-yaqooloona sab'atunw Wa-saaminuhum kalbuhum; qur Rabbeee a'lamu bi'iddatihim maa ya'lamuhum illaa qaleel; falaa tumaari feehim illaa miraaa'an zaahiranw Wa-laa tastafti feehim minhum ahadaa

23.t: And never say of anything, “I will definitely do this tomorrow,”
23.tr: Wa-laa taqoolanna lishai'in innee faa'ilun zaalika ghadaa

24.t: without adding, “if Allah so wills!” But if you forget, then remember your Lord, and say, “I trust my Lord will guide me to what is more right than this.”
24.tr: Illaaa aien yashaaa'al laah; wazkur Rabbaka izaa naseeta Wa-qul 'asaaa any yahdiyani Rabbee li-aqraba min haazaa rashadaa

25.t: They had remained in their cave for three hundred years, adding nine
25.tr: Wa-labisoo fee kahfihim salaasa mi'atin sineena wazdaadoo tis'aa

26.t: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah knows best how long they stayed. With Him ˹alone˺ is ˹the knowledge of˺ the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How perfectly He hears and sees! They have no guardian besides Him, and He shares His command with none.”
26.tr: Qulil laahu a'lamu bimaa labisoo lahoo ghaibus samaawaati wal-ardi absir bihee Wa-asmi'; maa lahum min doonihee minw waliyyinw Wa-laa yushriku fee hukmihee ahadaa

27.t: Recite what has been revealed to you from the Book of your Lord. None can change His Words, nor can you find any refuge besides Him
27.tr: Watlu maaa oohiya ilaika min Kitaabi Rabbika laa mubaddila li-Kalimaatihee Wa-lan tajida min doonihee multahadaa

28.t: And patiently stick with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. Do not let your eyes look beyond them, desiring the luxuries of this worldly life. And do not obey those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follow ˹only˺ their desires and whose state is ˹total˺ loss
28.tr: Wasbir nafsaka ma'al lazeena yad'oona Rabbahum bilghadaati wal'ashiyyi yureedoona Wajhahoo Wa-laa ta'du 'aynaaka 'anhum tureedu zeenatal hayaatid dunyaa Wa-laa tuti' man aghfalnaa qalbahoo 'an zikrinaa wattaba'a hawaahu Wa-kaana amruhoo furutaa

29.t: And say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹This is˺ the truth from your Lord. Whoever wills let them believe, and whoever wills let them disbelieve.” Surely We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will ˹completely˺ surround them. When they cry for aid, they will be aided with water like molten metal, which will burn ˹their˺ faces. What a horrible drink! And what a terrible place to rest
29.tr: Wa-qulil haqqu mir Rabbikum faman shaaa'a falyu'minw Wa-man shaaa'a falyakfur; innaaa a'tadnaa lizzaalimeena Naaran ahaata bihim suraadiquhaa; Wa-ien yastagheesoo yughaasoo bimaaa'in kalmuhli yashwil wujooh' bi'sash sharaab; Wa-saaa'at murtafaqaa

30.t: As for those who believe and do good, We certainly never deny the reward of those who are best in deeds
30.tr: Innal lazeena aamanoo Wa-'amilus saalihaati innaa laa nudee'u ajra man ahsana 'amalaa

31.t: It is they who will have the Gardens of Eternity, with rivers flowing under their feet. There they will be adorned with bracelets of gold, and wear green garments of fine silk and rich brocade, reclining there on ˹canopied˺ couches. What a marvellous reward! And what a fabulous place to rest
31.tr: Ulaaa'ika lahum Jannaatu 'Adnin tajree min tahtihimul anhaaru yuhallawna feehaa min asaawira min zahabinw Wa-yalbasoona siyaaban khudram min sundusinw Wa-istabraqim muttaki'eena feehaa 'alal araaa'ik; ni'mas sawaab; Wa-hasunat murtafaqaa

32.t: Give them ˹O Prophet˺ an example of two men. To ˹the disbelieving˺ one We gave two gardens of grapevines, which We surrounded with palm trees and placed ˹various˺ crops in between
32.tr: Wadrib lahum masalar rajulaini ja'alnaa li-ahadihimaa jannataini min a'naabinw Wa-hafafnaahumaa binakhilinw Wa-ja'alnaa bainahumaa zar'aa

33.t: Each garden yielded ˹all˺ its produce, never falling short. And We caused a river to flow between them
33.tr: Kiltal jannataini aatat ukulahaa Wa-lam tazlim minhu shai'anw Wa-fajjarnaa khi-laalahumaa naharaa

34.t: And he had other resources ˹as well˺. So he boasted to a ˹poor˺ companion of his, while conversing with him, “I am greater than you in wealth and superior in manpower.”
34.tr: Wa-kaana lahoo samarun faqaala lisaahibihee Wa-huwa yuhaawiruhoo ana aksaru minka maalanw Wa-a'azzu nafaraa

35.t: And he entered his property, while wronging his soul, saying, “I do not think this will ever perish
35.tr: Wa-dakhala jannatahoo Wa-huwa zaalimul linafsihee qaala maaa azunnu an tabeeda haaziheee abadaa

36.t: nor do I think the Hour will ˹ever˺ come. And if in fact I am returned to my Lord, I will definitely get a far better outcome than ˹all˺ this.”
36.tr: Wa-maaa azunnus Saa'ata qaaa'imatanw Wa-la'ir rudittu ilaa Rabbee la-ajidanna khairam minhaa munqalabaa

37.t: His ˹believing˺ companion replied, while conversing with him, “Do you disbelieve in the One Who created you from dust, then ˹developed you˺ from a sperm-drop, then formed you into a man
37.tr: Qaala lahoo saahibuhoo Wa-huwa yuhaawiruhooo akafarta billazee khalaqaka min turaabin summa min nutfatin summa sawwaaka rajulaa

38.t: But as for me: He is Allah, my Lord, and I will never associate anyone with my Lord ˹in worship˺
38.tr: Laakinaa Huwal laahu Rabbee Wa-laa ushriku bi-Rabbeee ahadaa

39.t: If only you had said, upon entering your property, ‘This is what Allah has willed! There is no power except with Allah!’ Even though you see me inferior to you in wealth and offspring
39.tr: Wa-law-laaa iz dakhalta jannataka qulta maa shaaa'al laahu laa quwwata illaa billaah; in tarani ana aqalla minka maalanw Wa-waladaa

40.t: perhaps my Lord will grant me ˹something˺ better than your garden, and send down upon your garden a thunderbolt from the sky, turning it into a barren waste
40.tr: Fa'asaa Rabeee aien yu'tiyani khairam min jannatika Wa-yursila 'alaihaa husbaanam minas samaaa'i fatusbiha sa'eedan zalaqaa

41.t: Or its water may sink ˹into the earth˺, and then you will never be able to seek it out.”
41.tr: Aw yusbiha maaa'uhaaa ghawran falan tastatee'a lahoo talabaa

42.t: And so all his produce was ˹totally˺ ruined, so he started to wring his hands for all he had spent on it, while it had collapsed on its trellises. He cried, “Alas! I wish I had never associated anyone with my Lord ˹in worship˺!”
42.tr: Wa-uheeta bisamarihee faasbaha yuqallibu kaffaihi 'alaa maaa anfaqa feehaa Wa-hiya khaawiyatun 'alaa 'urooshihaa Wa-yaqoolu yaalaitanee lam ushrik bi-Rabbeee ahadaa

43.t: And he had no manpower to help him against Allah, nor could he ˹even˺ help himself
43.tr: Wa-lam takul lahoo fi'atuien yansuroonahoo min doonil laahi Wa-maa kaana muntasiraa

44.t: At this time, support comes ˹only˺ from Allah—the True ˹Lord˺. He is best in reward and best in outcome
44.tr: Hunaalikal walaayatu lillaahil haqq; huwa khairun sawaabanw Wa-khairun 'uqbaa

45.t: And give them a parable of this worldly life. ˹It is˺ like the plants of the earth, thriving when sustained by the rain We send down from the sky. Then they ˹soon˺ turn into chaff scattered by the wind. And Allah is fully capable of ˹doing˺ all things
45.tr: Wadrib lahum masalal hayaatid dunyaa kamaaa'in anzalnaahu minas samaaa'i fakhtalata bihee nabaatul ardi fa-asbaha hasheeman tazroo-hur riyaah; Wa-kaanal laahu 'alaa kulli shai'im muqtadiraa

46.t: Wealth and children are the adornment of this worldly life, but the everlasting good deeds are far better with your Lord in reward and in hope
46.tr: Almaalu walbanoona zeenatul hayaatid dunya wal-baaqiyaatus saalihaatu khairun 'inda Rabbika sawaabanw Wa-khairun amalaa

47.t: ˹Beware of˺ the Day We will blow the mountains away, and you will see the earth laid bare. And We will gather all ˹humankind˺, leaving none behind
47.tr: Wa-yawma nusaiyirul jibaala Wa-taral arda baariza-tanw Wa-hasharnaahum falam nughaadir minhum ahadaa

48.t: They will be presented before your Lord in rows, ˹and the deniers will be told,˺ “You have surely returned to Us ˹all alone˺ as We created you the first time, although you ˹always˺ claimed that We would never appoint a time for your return.”
48.tr: Wa 'uridoo 'alaa Rabbika saffaa, laqad ji'tumoonaa kamaa khalaqnaakum awala marrah; bal za'amtum allannaj'ala lakum maw'idaa

49.t: And the record ˹of deeds˺ will be laid ˹open˺, and you will see the wicked in fear of what is ˹written˺ in it. They will cry, “Woe to us! What kind of record is this that does not leave any sin, small or large, unlisted?” They will find whatever they did present ˹before them˺. And your Lord will never wrong anyone
49.tr: Wa-wudi'al kitaabu fataral mujrimeena mushfiqeena mimmaa feehi Wa-yaqooloona yaa-wailatanaa maa lihaazal kitaabi laa yughaadiru saghee-ratanw Wa-laa kabeeratan illaaa ahsaahaa; Wa-wajadoo maa 'amiloo haadiraa; Wa-laa yazlimu Rabbuka ahadaa

50.t: And ˹remember˺ when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” so they all did—but not Iblîs, who was one of the jinn, but he rebelled against the command of his Lord. Would you then take him and his descendants as patrons instead of Me, although they are your enemy? What an evil alternative for the wrongdoers ˹to choose˺
50.tr: Wa-iz qulnaa lilma-laaa'ikatis judoo li-Aadama fasajadooo illaaa Ibleesa kaana minal jinni fafasaqa 'an amri Rabbih; afatattakhizoonahoo Wa-zurriyatahooo awliyaaa'a min doonee Wa-hum lakum 'aduww; bi'sa lizzaalimeena badalaa

51.t: I never called them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth or ˹even˺ their own creation, nor would I take the misleaders as helpers
51.tr: Maaa ash-hattuhum khalqas samaawaati wal-ardi Wa-laa khalqa anfusihim Wa-maa kuntu muttakhizal mudilleena 'adudaa

52.t: And ˹beware of˺ the Day He will say, “Call upon those you claimed were My associate-gods.” So they will call them, but will receive no response. And We will make them ˹all˺ share in the same doom
52.tr: Wa-Yawma yaqoolu naadoo shurakaaa'i yal-lazeena za'amtum fada'awhum falam yastajeeboo lahum Wa-ja'alnaa bainahum maw-biqaa

53.t: The wicked will see the Fire and realize that they are bound to fall into it, and will find no way to avoid it
53.tr: Wa-ra al-mujrimoonan Naara fazannooo annahum muwaaqi'oohaa Wa-lam yajidoo 'anhaa masrifaa

54.t: We have surely set forth in this Quran every ˹kind of˺ lesson for people, but humankind is the most argumentative of all beings
54.tr: Wa-laqad sarrafnaa fee haazal quraani linnaasi min kulli masal; Wa-kaanal insaanu aksara shai'in jadalaa

55.t: And nothing prevents people from believing when guidance comes to them and from seeking their Lord’s forgiveness except ˹their demand˺ to meet the same fate of earlier deniers or that the torment would confront them face to face
55.tr: Wa-maa mana'an naasa any yu'minooo iz jaaa'ahumul hudaa Wa-yastaghfiroo Rabbahum illaaa an taatiyahum sunnatul awwaleena aw yaatiyahumul 'azaabu qubulaa

56.t: We do not send the messengers except as deliverers of good news and warners. But the disbelievers argue in falsehood, ˹hoping˺ to discredit the truth with it, and make a mockery of My revelations and warnings
56.tr: Wa-maa nursilul mursaleena illaa mubashshireena Wa-munzireen; Wa-yujaadilul lazeena kafaroo bilbaatili liyudhidoo bihil haqqa wattakhazooo Aayaatee Wa-maaa unziroo huzuwaa

57.t: And who does more wrong than those who, when reminded of their Lord’s revelations, turn away from them and forget what their own hands have done? We have certainly cast veils over their hearts—leaving them unable to comprehend this ˹Quran˺—and deafness in their ears. And if you ˹O Prophet˺ invite them to ˹true˺ guidance, they will never be ˹rightly˺ guided
57.tr: Wa-man azlamu mimman zukkira bi-ayaati Rabbihee fa-a'rada 'anhaa Wa-nasiya maa qaddamat yadaah; innaa ja'alnaa 'alaa quloobihim akinnatan any yafqahoohu Wa-feee aazaanihim waqraa; Wa-in tad'uhum ilal hudaa falany yahtadooo izan abadaa

58.t: Your Lord is the All-Forgiving, Full of Mercy. If He were to seize them ˹immediately˺ for what they commit, He would have certainly hastened their punishment. But they have an appointed time, from which they will find no refuge
58.tr: Wa-Rabbukal Ghafooru zur rahmati law yu'aakhi-zuhum bimaa kasaboo la'ajala lahumul 'azaab; bal lahum maw'idul laien yajidoo min doonihee maw'ilaa

59.t: Those ˹are the˺ societies We destroyed when they persisted in wrong, and We had set a time for their destruction
59.tr: Wa-tilkal quraaa ahlak-nahum lammaa zulamoo Wa-ja'alnaa limahlikihim maw'idaa

60.t: And ˹remember˺ when Moses said to his young assistant, “I will never give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if I travel for ages.”
60.tr: Wa-iz qaalaa Moosaa lifataahu laaa abrahu hattaaa ablugha majma'al bahrayni aw amdiya huqubaa

61.t: But when they ˹finally˺ reached the point where the seas met, they forgot their ˹salted˺ fish, and it made its way into the sea, slipping away ˹wondrously˺
61.tr: Falammaa balaghaa majma'a bainihimaa nasiyaa hootahumaa fattakhaza sabeelahoo fil bahri sarabaa

62.t: When they had passed further, he said to his assistant, “Bring us our meal! We have certainly been exhausted by today’s journey.”
62.tr: Falammaa jaawazaa qaala lifataahu aatinaa ghadaaa'anaa laqad laqeena min safarinaa haazaa nasabaa

63.t: He replied, “Do you remember when we rested by the rock? ˹That is when˺ I forgot the fish. None made me forget to mention this except Satan. And the fish made its way into the sea miraculously.”
63.tr: Qaala ara'ayta iz awainaaa ilas sakhrati fa-innee naseetul hoota Wa-maaa ansaaneehu illash Shaitaanu an azkurah; wattakhaza sabeelahoo fil bahri 'ajabaa

64.t: Moses responded, “That is ˹exactly˺ what we were looking for.” So they returned, retracing their footsteps
64.tr: Qaala zaalika maa kunnaa nabghi; fartaddaa 'alaa aasaari-him-maa qasasaa

65.t: There they found a servant of Ours, to whom We had granted mercy from Us and enlightened with knowledge of Our Own
65.tr: Fa-wajadaa 'abdam min 'ibaadinaaa aatainaahu Rahmatam min 'indinaa Wa-'allamnaahu mil ladunnaa 'ilmaa

66.t: Moses said to him, “May I follow you, provided that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?”
66.tr: Qaala lahoo Moosaa hal attabi'uka 'alaaa an tu'allimani mimmaa 'ullimta rushdaa

67.t: He said, “You certainly cannot be patient ˹enough˺ with me
67.tr: Qaalaa innaka lan tastatee'a ma'iya sabraa

68.t: And how can you be patient with what is beyond your ˹realm of˺ knowledge?”
68.tr: Wa-kaifa tasbiru 'alaa maa lam tuhit bihee khubraa

69.t: Moses assured ˹him˺, “You will find me patient, Allah willing, and I will not disobey any of your orders.”
69.tr: Qaala satajiduneee in shaa 'al-laahu saabiranw Wa-laaa a'see laka amraa

70.t: He responded, “Then if you follow me, do not question me about anything until I ˹myself˺ clarify it for you.”
70.tr: Qaala fa-init taba'tanee falaa tas'alnee 'an shai'in hattaaa uhdisa laka minhu zikraa

71.t: So they set out, but after they had boarded a ship, the man made a hole in it. Moses protested, “Have you done this to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing!”
71.tr: Fantalaqaa hattaaa izaa rakibaa fis safeenati kharaqahaa qaala akharaqtahaa litughriqa ahlahaa laqad ji'ta shai'an imraa

72.t: He replied, “Did I not say that you cannot have patience with me?”
72.tr: Qaala alam aqul innaka lan tastatee'a ma'iya sabraa

73.t: Moses pleaded, “Excuse me for forgetting, and do not be hard on me.”
73.tr: Qaala laa tu'aakhiznee bimaa naseetu Wa-laa turhiqnee min amree 'usraa

74.t: So they proceeded until they came across a boy, and the man killed him. Moses protested, “Have you killed an innocent soul, who killed no one? You have certainly done a horrible thing.”
74.tr: Fantalaqaa hattaa izaa laqiyaa ghulaaman faqatalahoo qaala aqatalta nafsan zakiy-yatam bighairi nafs; laqad ji'ta shai'an nukraa

75.t: He answered, “Did I not tell you that you cannot have patience with me?”
75.tr: Qaala alam aqul laka innaka lan tastatee'a ma'iya sabraa

76.t: Moses replied, “If I ever question you about anything after this, then do not keep me in your company, for by then I would have given you enough of an excuse.”
76.tr: Qaala in sa-altuka 'an shai'im ba'dahaa falaa tusaahibnee qad balaghta mil ladunnee 'uzraa

77.t: So they moved on until they came to the people of a town. They asked them for food, but the people refused to give them hospitality. There they found a wall ready to collapse, so the man set it right. Moses protested, “If you wanted, you could have demanded a fee for this.”
77.tr: Fantalaqaa hattaaa izaaa atayaaa ahla qaryatinis tat'amaaa ahlahaa fa-abaw any yudaiyifoohumaa fawajadaa feehaa jidaarany yureedu any yanqadda fa-aqaamah; qaala law shi'ta lattakhazta 'alaihi ajraa

78.t: He replied, “This is the parting of our ways. I will explain to you what you could not bear patiently
78.tr: Qaala haazaa firaaqu bainee Wa-bainik; sa-unabi-'uka bitaaweeli maa lam tastati' 'alaihi sabraa

79.t: “As for the ship, it belonged to some poor people, working at sea. So I intended to damage it, for there was a ˹tyrant˺ king ahead of them who seizes every ˹good˺ ship by force
79.tr: Ammas safeenatu fakaanat limasaakeena ya'maloona fil bahri fa-arattu an a'eebahaa Wa-kaana waraaa'-ahum malikuien yaakhuzu kulla safeenatin ghasbaa

80.t: “And as for the boy, his parents were ˹true˺ believers, and we feared that he would pressure them into defiance and disbelief
80.tr: Wa-aammal ghulaamu fakaana abawaahu mu'minaini fakhasheenaaa aien yurhiqa-humaa tughyaananw Wa-kufraa

81.t: So we hoped that their Lord would give them another, more virtuous and caring in his place
81.tr: Faradnaa aien yubdila-humaa Rabbuhumaa khairam minhu zakaatanw Wa-aqraba ruhmaa

82.t: “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and under the wall was a treasure that belonged to them, and their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord willed that these children should come of age and retrieve their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it ˹all˺ on my own. This is the explanation of what you could not bear patiently.”
82.tr: Wa-ammal jidaaru fakaana lighulaamaini yateemaini fil madeenati Wa-kaana tahtahoo kanzul lahumaa Wa-kaana aboohumaa saalihan fa-araada Rabbuka any yablughaaa ashuddahumaa Wa-yastakhrijaa kanzahumaa rahmatam mir Rabbik; Wa-maa fa'altuhoo 'an amree; zaalika taaweelu maa lam tasti' 'alaihi sabra

83.t: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about Ⱬul-Qarnain. Say, “I will relate to you something of his narrative.”
83.tr: Wa-yas'aloonaka 'an Zil Qarnaini qul sa-atloo 'alaikum minhu zikraa

84.t: Surely We established him in the land, and gave him the means to all things
84.tr: Innaa makkannaa lahoo fil ardi Wa-aatainaahu min kulli shai'in sababaa

86.t: until he reached the setting ˹point˺ of the sun, which appeared to him to be setting in a spring of murky water, where he found some people. We said, “O Ⱬul-Qarnain! Either punish them or treat them kindly.”
86.tr: Hattaaa izaa balagha maghribash shamsi wajadahaaa taghrubu fee 'aynin hami'a-tinw Wa-wajada 'indahaa qawmaa; qulnaa yaa-Zal Qarnaini immaaa an tu'az-ziba Wa-immaaa an tattakhiza feehim husnaa

87.t: He responded, “Whoever does wrong will be punished by us, then will be returned to their Lord, Who will punish them with a horrible torment
87.tr: Qaala amma man zalama fasawfa nu'azzibuhoo summa yuraddu ilaa Rabbihee fa-yu-'azzibuhoo azaaban nukraa

88.t: As for those who believe and do good, they will have the finest reward, and we will assign them easy commands.”
88.tr: Wa-ammaa man aamana Wa-'amila saalihan falahoo jazaaa'anil husnaa Wa-sanaqoolu lahoo min amrinaa yusraa

90.t: until he reached the rising ˹point˺ of the sun. He found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it
90.tr: Hattaaa izaa balagha matli'ash shamsi wajdahaa tatlu'u alaa qawmil lam naj'al lahum min doonihaa sitraa

91.t: So it was. And We truly had full knowledge of him
91.tr: Kazaalika Wa-qad ahatnaa bimaa ladaihi khubraa

93.t: until he reached ˹a pass˺ between two mountains. He found in front of them a people who could hardly understand ˹his˺ language
93.tr: Hattaaa izaa balagha bainas saddaini wajada min doonihimaa qawmal laa yakaa-doona yafqahoona qawlaa

94.t: They pleaded, “O Ⱬul-Qarnain! Surely Gog and Magog are spreading corruption throughout the land. Should we pay you tribute, provided that you build a wall between us and them?”
94.tr: Qaaloo yaa-Zal qarnaini inna Yaajooja Wa-Maajooja mufsidoona fil ardi fahal naj'alu laka kharjan 'alaaa an taj'ala bainanaa Wa-bainahum saddaa

95.t: He responded, “What my Lord has provided for me is far better. But assist me with resources, and I will build a barrier between you and them
95.tr: Qaala maa makkannee feehi Rabbee khairun fa-a'eenoonee biquwwatin aj'al bainakum Wa-bainahum radmaa

96.t: Bring me blocks of iron!” Then, when he had filled up ˹the gap˺ between the two mountains, he ordered, “Blow!” When the iron became red hot, he said, “Bring me molten copper to pour over it.”
96.tr: Aatoonee zubaral hadeed, hattaaa izaa saawaa bainas sadafaini qaalan fukhoo hattaaa izaa ja'alahoo naaran qaala aatooneee ufrigh 'alaihi qitraa

97.t: And so the enemies could neither scale nor tunnel through it
97.tr: Famas taa'ooo aien yazharoohu Wa-mas tataa'oo lahoo naqbaa

98.t: He declared, “This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will level it to the ground. And my Lord’s promise is ever true.”
98.tr: Qaala haaza rahmatum mir Rabbee fa-izaa jaaa'a wa'du Rabbee ja'alahoo dakkaaa'a; Wa-kaana; Wa-du Rabbee haqqaa

99.t: On that Day, We will let them surge ˹like waves˺ over one another. Later, the Trumpet will be blown, and We will gather all ˹people˺ together
99.tr: Wa-taraknaa ba'dahum Yawma'izien yamooju fee ba'dinw Wa-nufikha fis Soori fajama'naahum jam'aa

100.t: On that Day We will display Hell clearly for the disbelievers

101.t: those who turned a blind eye to My Reminder and could not stand listening ˹to it˺
101.tr: Allazeena kaanat a'yunuhum fee ghitaaa'in 'an zikree Wa-kaanoo la yastatee'oona sam'aa

102.t: Do the disbelievers think they can ˹simply˺ take My servants as lords instead of Me? We have surely prepared Hell as an accommodation for the disbelievers
102.tr: Afahasibal lazeena kafarooo aien yattakhizoo 'ibaadee min dooneee awliyaaa'; innaaa a'tadnaa jahannama lil-kaafireena nuzulaa

103.t: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall we inform you of who will lose the most deeds

104.t: ˹They are˺ those whose efforts are in vain in this worldly life, while they think they are doing good!”
104.tr: Allazeena dalla sa'yuhum fil hayaatid dunyaa Wa-hum yahsaboona annahum yuhsinoona sun'aa

105.t: It is they who reject the signs of their Lord and their meeting with Him, rendering their deeds void, so We will not give their deeds any weight on Judgment Day
105.tr: Ulaaa'ikal lazeena kafaroo bi-aayaati Rabbihim Wa-liqaaa'ihee fahabitat a'maaluhum falaa nuqeemu lahum Yawmal Qiyaamati waznaa

106.t: That is their reward: Hell, for their disbelief and mockery of My signs and messengers
106.tr: Zaalika jazaaa'uhum jahannamu bimaa kafaroo wattakhazooo Aayaatee Wa-Rusulee huzuwaa

107.t: Indeed, those who believe and do good will have the Gardens of Paradise as an accommodation
107.tr: Innal lazeena aamanoo Wa-'amilus saalihaati kaanat lahum Jannaatul Firdawsi nuzulaa

108.t: where they will be forever, never desiring anywhere else

109.t: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If the ocean were ink for ˹writing˺ the Words of my Lord, it would certainly run out before the Words of my Lord were finished, even if We refilled it with its equal.”
109.tr: Qul law kaanal bahru midaadal li-kalimaati Rabbee lanafidal bahru qabla an tanfada Kalimaatu Rabbee Wa-law ji'naa bimislihee madadaa

110.t: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a man like you, ˹but˺ it has been revealed to me that your God is only One God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with their Lord, let them do good deeds and associate none in the worship of their Lord.”
110.tr: Qul innamaaa ana basharum mislukum yoohaaa ilaiya annamaa ilaahukum Ilaahunw Waahid; faman kaana yarjoo liqaaa'a Rabbihee falya'mal 'amalan saalihanw Wa-laa yushrik bi'ibaadati Rabbiheee ahadaa
